text: KEPT ON PURPOSE, against the move that took its two neighbours out. This record shares their identity - brand "unknown", model "unknown" - and it is not the same kind of thing. Its source says so: « Not a device. The record the engine uses when the driver reports an identity no record matches and the listener has not said. » It is the TERMINAL of the cascade, the bottom a consumer resolves to when nothing else matches, and deleting it would remove the floor rather than a duplicate. akm-generique and ess-generique were chip defaults wearing a device; this one is the absence of a device, which is a role no chip family can fill.
what_is_doubtful: Its `kind` says "dac", which is the one field that is plainly wrong: it is not a converter, it is the answer "we do not know which converter". And it carries dsd_direct false where its chip family says "unknown" - both end in the conservative branch, so nothing breaks, but two levels still disagree. The real question is whether a terminal belongs in devices/ at all, or whether a consumer should get it from the vocabulary instead of from a record that has to pretend to be a device to exist.
